rv.q: Transferred from London’s West End by way of Cambridge, Mass., this twinkly two-hander delivers lavishly on the promise of a rom-com: laughter, escape and fantasy.

The show's minimalism extends to its set by Soutra Gilmour: two oversize piles of luggage on a turntable—conceptually clever even if it may trigger unpleasant memories of long, foot-tapping waits at airport carousels.
The guy takes a Costco sirloin and turns it into Peter Luger.
When Two Strangers does do that, it does achieve something magical, and those moments make you see what a smaller-scale musical can do successfully without a huge budget or soapy showmanship.
So while this show held me for Act 1 with its considerable charm, by Act 2, it was hitting turbulence.
As the icing on the cake, not only have they fallen in love with each other but we’ve fallen in love with them as well.
Most of all, I can think of no two people better equipped to carry this delightful musical than Sam Tutty and Christiani Pitts.
Two Strangers (Carry a Cake Across New York) is a sweet, original musical about finding love in the Big Apple.
Tutty and Pitts do just that and make Two Strangers a terrific feel-good addition to this theater season.
And Two Strangers (Carry a Cake Across New York) definitely works.

Tutty’s appealing looks, pure voice, comic instincts, and obvious acting skills, and somehow resemblance to a living Teletubby make him the huge plus for a vital Two Strangers (Carry a Cake Across New York) run.
This is a show so charming, so adorable, that you can easily overlook its flaws.
This would be a thumbs up date night show no matter your age.
Infectiously whimsical and sentimental, the show juxtaposes these qualities against a New York reality that has little time for either.

What I found most surprising about this modest, appealing two-person musical, whose title more or less sums up what happens, was the reaction to it on the night I attended – the ecstatic cheers at the start; the mobbed stage door afterwards.
Whatever, the cases look imposingly ugly, and act as a creative handcuffs on the show.
The trouble is, that's often an apt description of the show itself, too.
But I should've known from its twee little title that this would not be for me, and I was unfortunately correct.
As meet-cutes go, this one turns very problematic in Act 2, if not before.
It's also one of the best new musicals of the year.
In a season crowded with gaudy overindulgence, this small, sweet musical carries its multi-layered cake with surprising elegance.
Utterly charming and winsomely quirky, this show evokes laughter and joy in equal measures, while also contending with moments of substance and painful truth.
A sweet slice of musical patisserie for those partial to sugar.
If you are looking for great structure and exhilarating drama, look elsewhere.
In fairness, the book offers plenty of laughs, thanks in large part to endearing performances by Tutty and Pitts.
Happily, the charming new Broadway musical Two Strangers (Carry a Cake Across New York) gets things right.
Warm, witty, and easy to enjoy.

cn.t: Critics find this charming British rom-com a modest, sweet confection elevated by its two leads, though some dismiss it as slight and formulaic. The twee two-hander divides opinion but wins over most with sincerity and heart.

Two Strangers is easily the early frontrunner for next year's Best Musical. It's a real charmer that has all the makings of a hit — good music, lovely performances, emotional substance, and maybe most charming of all, it's unexpected.
I recommend this thoroughly to just about anyone who loves New York theater... I love the show.
